GENERATED MEMO:
# INVESTMENT MEMORANDUM

**TO:** Investment Committee  
**FROM:** Private Credit Team  
**DATE:** [Current Date]  
**RE:** MSP Recovery / Hazel Partners Third Amendment Summary

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Date of Agreement:** August 2, 2024

**Borrower / Company Overview:**  
Subrogation Holdings, LLC (Delaware LLC) serves as the borrower, with MSP Recovery, LLC (Florida LLC) as the ultimate parent entity. MSP Recovery operates in the claims recovery business, focusing on healthcare claim subrogation and recovery rights.

**Transaction Description:**  
This transaction represents a third amendment summary to an existing Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated November 10, 2023. The structure involves Hazel Partners Holdings LLC as both lender and administrative agent, with multiple related entities as credit parties including various MSP Recovery subsidiaries.

**Purpose of Financing:**  
The financing provides an "Operational Collection Floor" facility to support MSP Recovery's working capital needs and specifically enables the purchase of certain redacted claims. The facility is structured as Term Loan B advances with original issue discount.

**Company Background:**  
MSP Recovery operates through a complex organizational structure involving multiple series LLCs and subsidiaries focused on healthcare claims recovery. The company maintains operations from Coral Gables, Florida under the leadership of CEO John Ruiz.

---

## 2. INVESTMENT HIGHLIGHTS & RISKS

**Key Strengths / Credit Positives:**
• Secured facility with comprehensive collateral package including claims assets and membership interests
• Priority repayment structure with Operational Collection Floor advances taking precedence over Term Loan A and Term Loan B
• Upside participation rights for lender (50% of collections up to $8MM, then 25% thereafter)
• Structured draw schedule limits rapid capital deployment risk (maximum once per month draws)
• Independent operating committee governance provides additional oversight
• Real estate collateral release mechanism tied to specific repayment milestones

**Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:**
• **Asset Concentration Risk:** Heavy reliance on healthcare claims recovery performance in single industry vertical
• **Regulatory/Legal Risk:** Claims recovery business subject to healthcare regulation and litigation outcomes  
• **Liquidity Risk:** Complex multi-tranche draw structure may create timing mismatches; *Mitigated by monthly draw limitations and structured release provisions*
• **Counterparty Risk:** Dependence on third-party performance for claims processing and collections
• **Structural Complexity:** Multiple entity structure creates operational and administrative complexity; *Mitigated by comprehensive security documentation across all entities*

---

## 3. KEY DEAL TERMS

| **Term** | **Details** |
|----------|-------------|
| **Deal Size** | $16,000,000 maximum aggregate Operational Collection Floor |
| **Deal Price** | N/A (Original issue discount mentioned but amount not specified) |
| **Interest Rate** | N/A |
| **Maturity Date** | N/A |
| **Payment Frequency** | N/A |
| **Draw Schedule** | Eight tranches of $1,750,000 (July 2024 - September 2025) plus additional $2,000,000 by August 31, 2024 |
| **Key Covenants** | Priority repayment of Operational Collection Floor over Term Loans A&B; Mortgage and Guaranty release upon full OCF repayment or by December 31, 2024 |
| **Collateral** | Claims assets, membership interests of New Claims Subsidiary, real estate mortgage, guaranty agreements |
| **Upside Participation** | 50% of collections until $8MM recovered, then 25% thereafter |

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Date of Agreement:** August 2, 2024

**Borrower / Company Overview:**  
Subrogation Holdings, LLC (Delaware LLC) serves as the borrower, with MSP Recovery, LLC (Florida LLC) as the ultimate parent entity. MSP Recovery operates in the claims recovery business, focusing on healthcare claim subrogation and recovery rights.

**Transaction Description:**  
This transaction represents a third amendment summary to an existing Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated November 10, 2023. The structure involves Hazel Partners Holdings LLC as both lender and administrative agent, with multiple related entities as credit parties including various MSP Recovery subsidiaries.

**Purpose of Financing:**  
The financing provides an "Operational Collection Floor" facility to support MSP Recovery's working capital needs and specifically enables the purchase of certain redacted claims. The facility is structured as Term Loan B advances with original issue discount.

**Company Background:**  
MSP Recovery operates through a complex organizational structure involving multiple series LLCs and subsidiaries focused on healthcare claims recovery. The company maintains operations from Coral Gables, Florida under the leadership of CEO John Ruiz.

## 2. INVESTMENT HIGHLIGHTS & RISKS

**Key Strengths / Credit Positives:**
• Secured facility with comprehensive collateral package including claims assets and membership interests
• Priority repayment structure with Operational Collection Floor advances taking precedence over Term Loan A and Term Loan B
• Upside participation rights for lender (50% of collections up to $8MM, then 25% thereafter)
• Structured draw schedule limits rapid capital deployment risk (maximum once per month draws)
• Independent operating committee governance provides additional oversight
• Real estate collateral release mechanism tied to specific repayment milestones

**Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:**
• **Asset Concentration Risk:** Heavy reliance on healthcare claims recovery performance in single industry vertical
• **Regulatory/Legal Risk:** Claims recovery business subject to healthcare regulation and litigation outcomes  
• **Liquidity Risk:** Complex multi-tranche draw structure may create timing mismatches; *Mitigated by monthly draw limitations and structured release provisions*
• **Counterparty Risk:** Dependence on third-party performance for claims processing and collections
• **Structural Complexity:** Multiple entity structure creates operational and administrative complexity; *Mitigated by comprehensive security documentation across all entities*
